definition: RL methods that optimize the policy directly by gradient ascent on expected reward — REINFORCE through actor-critic and PPO.
details: RL methods that optimize the policy directly by gradient ascent on expected reward — REINFORCE through actor-critic and PPO.

explainer.lead: Policy gradient methods optimize a policy directly by gradient ascent on expected reward, spanning REINFORCE through actor-critic and PPO. They underpin much of modern reinforcement learning.

tiers.eli5: The agent tweaks its own rulebook a little after each attempt so that better-scoring actions become more likely.
tiers.practitioner: Practitioners pick among REINFORCE, actor-critic, and PPO depending on variance and sample budget, and use PPO widely for stable training. A pitfall is unstable updates when the step size or variance control is badly chosen.
tiers.paperLevel: The policy parameters are updated by ascending an estimate of the gradient of expected reward, from the basic REINFORCE estimator to actor-critic and PPO variants. Estimator variance and step size govern stability and convergence.

explainer.example: PPO trains an agent on a control task by repeatedly taking gradient steps on the policy using reward-weighted updates.
